objective: Take the transposed-Jacobian defect to publishable depth against the discrete-adjoint consistency literature, and separately produce the lab's first frozen-turbulence error bound on one case, so the adjoint-methods claim rests on a written theory chapter and a measured number rather than on nine internal records
rationale: The defect is measured to an unusual standard and has never been set against the theory that would make it a contribution. Nine internal records carry it: the same adjoint vector satisfies its own decomposed operator to 1.2e-03 and leaves a residual of 329 times the right-hand side under the serial operator, independently reproduced at 328.8, against a serial floor of 1.14e-04, so one vector is judged by two operators five orders apart; the error across the rank sweep is not monotone in rank but keyed to the partitioner, with one decomposition landing at 0.00054 percent and another at 8.95 percent; 13 of the 15 largest residual entries sit on partition-boundary cells with the largest at 42.2; the right-hand side and the primal are invariant to within 4.8e-06 and 3.6e-06, and the mesh-warping leg is exonerated to 6e-09. The novelty sweep across 10 venues returned 63 negative searches. The literature position is the part that is written down but not yet argued: the two published sub-tenth-percent accuracy figures attach to the earlier explicit coloured-finite-difference architecture, while the matrix-free reverse-mode family has exactly one published accuracy measurement and it is serial by construction, which is precisely the gap a consistency-theory treatment should name. The honest limits belong in the same chapter: every defective measurement still sits on one background mesh, one co-ingredient hypothesis cannot be separated within the case, and the doctrine that decomposition invariance certifies consistency rather than correctness is the finding a reader should leave with. The frozen-turbulence half is a separate and currently empty claim: no bound exists anywhere, the ladder rung that would produce one is recorded as not yet run, and the route is recorded as structurally unavailable to field inversion because the correction field being solved for lives inside the turbulence model. That does not block the bound for a shape derivative, which is where it should be measured. Axis A: reading-kind, with the measured half priced from the same case's own arms. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured on this case: the five deciding arms of the decomposition discriminator campaign cost 12.80 core-min on the 2,777-cell coarse case, and a frozen-turbulence adjoint plus the full adjoint on the same case at the same rank count is that same class of work, so 25 core-min covers both arms plus one repeat; the write-up half spends nothing, and the campaign's own 26 percent overrun is disclosed here rather than smoothed away, it sat entirely in an unrunnable arm that this item does not repeat
expected_knowledge_gain: Two deliverables with separable outcomes. On the write-up: either the consistency theory explains the partitioner keying, in which case the defect is an instance of a known consistency failure and the contribution is the measurement plus the identification, or it does not, in which case the contribution is a documented consistency failure the theory does not cover, which is a stronger claim and a heavier evidential burden that the chapter must state. On the bound: the frozen-turbulence gradient is compared against the full adjoint gradient on a case whose full gradient is verified against finite differences, so the difference is the bound. Either it is small, and frozen turbulence becomes an admissible cheap mode with a stated error, or it is large, and the lab has a number to cite the next time somebody proposes it, which today it does not.
sequencing: Ride-along under strategy rule 4 for the write-up half, which spends nothing. The bound arm rides the same coarse case the discriminator campaign already used and queues behind Ladder V under rule 1.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Adjoint methods deep expertise: Giles & Pierce papers + discrete-adjoint consistency theory -> PROOF: the transposed-Jacobian defect written up at publishable depth; frozen-turbulence error bounded on one case.' Operationalised in two halves, both required. Half one: a chapter that states the defect against the consistency literature, carries the cross-residual and rank-sweep evidence with its independent reproduction, positions it against the one published serial accuracy measurement for this architecture, and states its own limits plainly, naming the single-mesh confound, the unseparated co-ingredient, and the invariance-is-not-correctness doctrine. A chapter that omits any of the three limits fails. Half two: a number, the relative difference between the frozen-turbulence adjoint gradient and the full adjoint gradient on one named case whose full gradient is already verified against finite differences, reported component by component with the verification status of each component stated, and reported as a bound rather than as an error estimate.
